## Fault Injection and Recovery in LLM Training

A benchmark called RFT-FaultBench was built on top of the OpenRLHF training framework and instantiated on a controlled arithmetic-style reasoning task, providing a reproducible environment for systematic fault injection and anomaly analysis.

The system must first detect abnormal behavior, then determine what has gone wrong, and finally trigger targeted recovery actions, treating failure handling as a structured failure-management problem rather than as purely ad hoc debugging.

## SFT vs. Reinforcement Learning Approaches

Unlike supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which requires high-quality labeled data and learns via direct instruction, RFT allows models to explore action spaces and learn from reward signals, enabling adaptation in settings where ground truth annotations are scarce or ambiguous.

Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) fits best when you can provide clear target behaviors through demonstrations, or instruction-response pairs, and is great for teaching format and style.

## Recovery and Exploration

SFT policies struggle to recover once they deviate from expert trajectories, whereas methods using process reward models actively interact with the environment to correct mistakes.

In practice, SFT and RL are not mutually exclusive, and a hybrid strategy is often employed, using a high-quality set of demonstrations to teach the chat template, tool-calling format, and general readability, which helps RL avoid wasting time trying to learn the format of your dataset.

## AgenTracer: Overview

AgenTracer addresses failures in Large Language Model (LLM)-based agentic systems that, while more sophisticated than monolithic agents, are more prone to system failure. The research focuses on pinpointing the specific agent or step responsible for an error within long execution traces, defining the task of agentic system failure attribution.

## The Problem It Solves

Current state-of-the-art reasoning LLMs remain strikingly inadequate for this challenge, with accuracy generally below 10%.

## The Solution

AgenTracer is the first automated framework for annotating failed multi-agent trajectories via counterfactual replay and programmed fault injection. The framework applies programmatic fault injection to successful trajectories and counterfactual corrections to failed ones to identify the decisive error step, yielding 2,000+ trajectory–error step pairs, collectively referred to as TracerTraj-2.5K.

## AgenTracer-8B Model

AgenTracer-8B is a lightweight failure tracer trained with multi-granular reinforcement learning, capable of efficiently diagnosing errors in verbose multi-agent interactions. On the Who&When benchmark, AgenTracer-8B outperforms giant proprietary LLMs like Gemini-2.5-Pro and Claude-4-Sonnet by up to 18.18%.

The paper (arXiv 2509.03312) was published in September 2025 and is available on arXiv and OpenReview.
